scoreRule: One point per correct answer; ten points maximum. Provisional local result only.
description: Original English B2 independent Reading draft with ten inference and transfer questions; requires later pedagogical review.

tabs.title: Understanding Lena
tabs.description: Interpret her emotional situation and the changing friendship.

tabs.title: Evidence and Purpose
tabs.description: Identify why Lena chooses particular stories.

tabs.title: Responding Thoughtfully
tabs.description: Apply the message to communication across distance.

questions.q: Why does Lena think her photos have failed to tell Alex the whole story?
choices: They were taken in places Alex has already visited.
They reveal too much about her host family's working hours.
They present attractive experiences while leaving her loneliness hidden.
They show that she has lost interest in her exchange year.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: What changes when Lena listens to another newcomer's description of bus routes?
choices: She decides that public transport is too complicated to use.
She begins to see her own confusion as a shared experience rather than personal failure.
She learns she needs a certificate before joining the radio station.
She realises that the other volunteers are equally bad at recording.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: What does the bakery owner's story add to Lena's developing understanding of belonging?
choices: A successful business automatically prevents loneliness.
The main challenge for every newcomer is finding familiar food.
People who move abroad generally prefer to live alone.
Knowing a language may not remove the feeling of being excluded from unspoken rules.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: Why does Lena mention that her radio work is unpaid?
choices: To contrast the value of real conversations with a formal reward.
To suggest the station should stop interviewing immigrants.
To show that volunteering is required for exchange students.
To explain why she wants to leave Rotterdam early.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: How do the phone calls after the bakery interview support Lena's conclusion?
choices: They confirm that the bakery owner was unhappy with the interview.
They suggest that the programme became popular because it offered recipes.
They show that other people recognised feelings they had not openly discussed.
They prove that loneliness can be measured by the number of listeners.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: Why does finding the old school photo lead Lena to rethink her messages?
choices: It reminds her that their friendship once included honest conversations about difficulty.
It convinces her that Alex has forgotten their friendship.
It makes her question whether they ever enjoyed school together.
It prompts her to plan another set of cheerful photographs.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: What is the effect of Lena's admission that Alex may have felt left out?
choices: It implies Alex should have contacted her host family instead.
It acknowledges a possible consequence of her behaviour without blaming Alex.
It treats the distance between them as impossible to overcome.
It asks Alex to apologise for not responding to every photo.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: Alex cannot afford the train ticket. Which response would best match Lena's invitation?
choices: Cancel the conversation because the visit was the only option.
Ask Lena to send more photos until money is available.
Treat the invitation as a promise that Lena would pay all expenses.
Suggest a regular call instead of assuming the friendship must wait.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: Someone posts only happy pictures during an exchange year. What would Lena's experience suggest before judging that person's life?
choices: Photos are reliable proof that everyone is having a good time.
Public updates may omit difficulties that are not easy to share.
People who study abroad are usually less lonely than friends at home.
Posts should be understood as an invitation to compare achievements.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.

questions.q: Which reply from Alex would best support the conversation Lena now wants?
choices: Send a picture without discussing how either of them feels.
Promise to visit even if travel is impossible.
Avoid mentioning any problems so the exchange year feels successful.
Share honestly how college is going and suggest a workable time to talk.
questions.explanation: Lena connects the incident to her discovery that honest conversation and belonging matter more than attractive public updates.
